summary: find searches for the first occurrence of a substring and returns its zero-based starting position.
documentation: find searches for the first occurrence of a substring and returns its zero-based starting position. It returns -1 when there is no occurrence. The optional start and end parameters can restrict the search without changing returned indices.
inputs: An object with text and needle strings.
caution: Index zero is a successful match and is falsey in a Boolean context. Compare with -1 rather than testing the index directly.
scenarios: Locate a separator before splitting a legacy record.
Highlight the first search result in a preview.
Find an expected marker in a local import line.
title: Locate a substring
problem: Input is {text, needle}. Return the first position of needle in text, or -1 if absent. An empty needle matches at position zero, including in empty text.
goal: Use str.find() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Return text.find(needle) without converting the result to bool.
